chapter: George Lewis and the 1946 Jazz Foundation concert
title: Playing with George Lewis and the St. Bernard dances for Father Oswald
summary: Williams recalls playing with George Lewis around 1945 and the band for Father Oswald's school dances in St. Bernard Parish, with Lawrence Marrero, Slow Drag, Paul Barnes and Eulie Young.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well, anyway, we never did really talk about when you started with Joyce Lewis. Was that, you know what time that was about? I remember you played for the National Jazz Foundation on the wagon.
I remember that. I remember when that happened. I remember with George and I was playing with George in 45.
Had you been playing with him long before you went on that wagon or you just started with him?
No, no. I remember playing with him in between time because I got a book here. Paul Barnes was in the army. And I built this school. You might get some of it out of here.
Yeah.
This school down... In St. Bernard?
Yeah, in St. Bernard Parish. We got that.
Yeah, we got that.
I read about that. You read about that. And at that time you were using Paul Barnes?
Paul Barnes, yeah.
See, Paul Barnes' wife was from down there. I was playing for Father Oswald. Which be down there practically every Saturday.

And who did you use in the band? What were you using in the band? George, George, Lawrence Moreira, Slow Dre, Paul Barnes, and Trumpet was Eulie Young. Oh yeah. You remember Eulie, eh? You remember Eulie, eh? You remember Eulie, eh? Yeah. You remember Eulie. You remember Eulie. Never knew him.
I heard plenty about him but I never knew him.
He's still around, huh?
Yeah, he's a plaster. He done play anymore. Where did he live anyhow? I don't know if he's across the lake or what, but I know where his people live at, his white people.

Eulie Young played a long way playing for a number of years. He's one of those boys from way, way, way back. Is he in his 60s you think? Eulie Young played a long way playing for a number of years. He's one of those boys from way, way, way back. Is he in his 60s you think?
Eulie Young played a long way playing for a long way playing for a long way. He's a boss plaster. Puny. And he's got off the horn.
Look a son of Henry. Yeah. He's got one long, but you wouldn't think it, the way he could blow that trumpet. Got one long. He's a boss plaster.
Puny.
And he's got off the horn. Look at Sonny Henry. Yeah.
Yeah, I saw that grand marshal later. Yeah. He lived uptown. Yeah. But the priest would put on the dance down there.
Yeah, Father Oswald. And we built that, see Paul was, then they took Paul and Barnes in the Navy. They drafted him in the Navy.
Yeah, I can see here he's playing clarinet and George is playing alto. Did George play much alto in those days? Well he played enough, you know.
He knowed it. Mostly he played clarinet or mostly alto at that time?
